c121.title: Dogs in the park
c121.story: On Sunday, Anna's family has a [[picnic]] in the park. They sit at a table in the old [[pavilion]]. A [[bulldog]], a [[beagle]] and a sleepy [[basset]] want their sandwiches. A lady walks by with a tiny [[chihuahua]] in her bag. Behind her, a small [[terrier]] barks at a white [[poodle]]. Max arrives with his [[husky]] and his aunt's [[collie]]. A friendly [[pit bull]] plays with a ball near the trees. Max's aunt's dog moves the others together by [[instinct]], like sheep. A vet tells them about a [[parasite]] from dirty pond water. So Anna's dad fills a clean bowl for the dogs. Before they go home, Max cleans up his dog's [[excrement]]. Everyone says the park looks nicer than before.

c122.title: Grandma's farm
c122.story: Anna and Max spend Saturday on Grandma's farm. The [[farmer]] next door waves to them from his field. He drives his big [[tractor]] over forty [[hectares|hectare]] of wheat. 'In America, that's about a hundred [[acres|acre]],' says Max. Grandma's old [[mule]] is slow, but very strong. It carries ten [[bushels|bushel]] of apples from the [[homestead]] to the road. Max brings the mule a [[gallon]] of water from the well. Behind the house, bees collect [[nectar]] from the flowers. Grandma never uses a [[pesticide]] in her garden. 'An [[insecticide]] kills bees too, and bees are my friends,' she says. Her new tree is a [[hybrid]] of a pear and an apple. 'I want to taste the first fruit!' says Max.

c123.title: Hiking in the Carpathians
c123.story: In July, Anna and Max go [[hiking]] in the Carpathian Mountains. They stay at a small [[camp]] near a high [[cliff]]. Max uses a [[compass]] to find the path to the [[peak]]. On the way, a cool [[breeze]] comes up from the [[canyon]]. They rest under an old [[cedar]] on big [[granite]] rocks. Higher up, they walk across a wide, green [[plateau]]. Anna photographs the local [[flora]] and [[fauna]]: flowers, moss and birds. Then they paddle a canoe across a quiet mountain lake. On the shore, Max finds a shiny piece of [[quartz]]. Near the lake, they meet boy scouts who love [[scouting]]. Together they climb a hill and see a [[panorama]] of the mountains. Anna smiles, 'Let's come back next summer!'

c124.title: National parks in America
c124.story: In August, Anna and Max visit Max's cousin, a park [[ranger]] in America. On the first morning, he shows them a [[grizzly]] fishing in a cold river. At night a [[coyote]] howls, and by morning a [[raccoon]] is in their trash. Later, they drive slowly while a herd of [[bison]] crosses the road. Max laughs at a small [[gopher]] that pops out of a hole in the grass. Then they fly north to Alaska and watch [[caribou]] walk across the tundra. In Nevada, a group of wild [[mustangs|mustang]] runs across the dry plains. Their last stop is a swamp in Florida, where an alligator lies in the sun. Every evening, Max's cousin warns them to stay on the trail because of [[cougars|cougar]]. 'Some people call it a [[puma]], but it's the same big cat,' he says. On the last night, he makes a fire from [[hickory]] wood, and they roast corn. Anna says it was the best trip of her life.

c126.title: A climate strike
c126.story: On Friday, Anna joins a [[climate]] strike with other students in the park. Max's sign says, 'I want to see the sky, not [[smog]]!' A girl named Sofia talks about the [[ozone]] layer and a melting [[iceberg]] in the Arctic. A teacher explains that farm cows produce [[methane]], and cars produce carbon dioxide. Some students ask about [[fracking]] and the water under the ground. Anna shares simple [[eco]] ideas, like bikes and reusable bags. A boy says a [[tornado]] once damaged his grandma's house. Sofia explains that a [[cyclone]] is a giant spinning storm over warm ocean water. 'Near Asia, people call the same storm a [[typhoon]],' she adds. A [[tsunami]] is different: it's a huge wave after an earthquake under the sea. Any of them can hurt a whole [[region]] at once. In the end, the group cleans the park together and plants three small trees.
